svg.text: INVENTORY — CLASS DESIGN (LLD)
THE FACADE + TWO SEAMS
Inventory — FACADE
inventory(): InventoryService · orders(): OrderService
two concerns, deliberately two interfaces
«interface» InventoryService
receiveStock(sku, wh, qty, reason)
reserve(sku, wh, qty, ref): ReservationId
commit(resId, reason) · release(resId, reason)
adjust(sku, wh, delta, reason) · transfer(sku, from, to, qty, reason)
getStock(sku, wh): StockSnapshot
reserve / commit / release = the whole design in 3 verbs
«interface» OrderService
placeOrder(user, items, address, paymentMethod): Order
confirmPayment(orderId, txnId) · cancelOrder(orderId, reason)
updateOrderStatus(orderId, status) · getOrder / getUserOrders
checkAvailability(sku, qty, address) · getDeliveryEstimate(address)
THE CORE — one lock per (sku, warehouse) cell
InMemoryInventoryService
entries: ConcurrentHashMap<Key, Entry>
reservations: ConcurrentHashMap<ReservationId, Reservation>
Key = (skuId, warehouseId) — equals + hashCode
Entry { long onHand; long reserved; final Object lock; }
a dedicated lock object per cell — not the Entry itself
Reservation { id, skuId, warehouseId, quantity } — immutable
getEntry(sku, wh) = entries.computeIfAbsent(new Key(…), Entry::new)
every quantity mutation runs inside synchronized (e.lock)
Math.addExact on every increase → overflow throws, never wraps
ConcurrentHashMap for LOOKUP, per-cell monitor for MUTATION ✓
two SKUs, or one SKU in two warehouses, never contend
release / commit remove from the reservations map FIRST,
then take the lock → a double-release is structurally impossible
honest: reservations have NO expiry — a reservation that is
never committed or released holds stock hostage forever
honest: every method takes a `reason`, and none of them
record it — the audit-log hook exists, the audit log does not
fix both: a TTL sweeper (see the airline hold model) + an append-only ledger
THE ORDER SIDE — the only caller of reserve/commit/release
InMemoryOrderService
inventoryService: InventoryService (injected)
orders / payments / users / products: ConcurrentHashMap
warehouses: BLR-A, BLR-B, MUM-A, DEL-A (hard-coded)
placeOrder → validate user + products, price the basket,
pick nearest warehouse, status = CREATED. No stock held yet.
confirmPayment → reserve() per line, stash the
ReservationId on the line item, status = CONFIRMED
cancelOrder → release() every reservation
updateOrderStatus(DELIVERED) → commit() every reservation
the ReservationId on the line item IS the link between
The value objects
SkuId · WarehouseId · ReservationId
OrderId · UserId · PaymentId · CategoryId
typed ids, not raw Strings — you cannot pass a
warehouse id where a sku is expected ✓
StockSnapshot
onHand · reserved
available() = onHand − reserved
taken under the cell lock, returned immutable
honest: it is stale the instant it is returned —
never branch on it, only reserve() decides
OrderStatus — where inventory verbs fire
CREATED → PAYMENT_PENDING → CONFIRMED → PICKING → PACKED → OUT_FOR_DELIVERY → DELIVERED
off-ramps: CANCELLED · FAILED
CONFIRMED = reserve · DELIVERED = commit · CANCELLED = release
honest: it is a plain enum — nothing rejects an illegal jump like CREATED → DELIVERED
THE ARITHMETIC — every verb, under the cell lock
the five mutations
receiveStock onHand += qty
reserve guard available ≥ qty; reserved += qty
release reserved −= qty
commit reserved −= qty AND onHand −= qty
adjust onHand += delta, floored at reserved
commit is the only verb that touches BOTH counters —
and it does so in one critical section, never two
transfer — the deadlock trap
two cells, so TWO locks must be held at once.
A→B and B→A running concurrently would
each hold what the other wants.
Fix: a GLOBAL ORDER on the locks.
compare warehouse ids as strings; always take
the lexicographically smaller one first.
a consistent order makes a lock CYCLE impossible —
the textbook answer, and one of the cheapest to say
the invariants it defends
0 ≤ reserved ≤ onHand — always
available = onHand − reserved ≥ 0
a cycle-count adjust cannot drop onHand
below what is already reserved
transfer moves only AVAILABLE units —
never someone else's reservation
underflow checks throw IllegalStateException, not silence
orders drive stock
all five verbs mutate the same two longs inside the cell

svg.text: WHITEBOARD ORDER:

① Inventory facade → two seams → ② InMemoryInventoryService: Key → Entry{onHand, reserved, lock} → ③ OrderService as the caller (CONFIRMED/DELIVERED/CANCELLED) → ④ the arithmetic, plus transfer's lock ordering
LEGEND

g.text: Patterns: Facade · Reserve-Commit-Release · per-cell locking · lock ordering · typed ids
Multi-warehouse inventory — no overselling under concurrent orders — LLD
